practice_description.medium: Installation, video, sculpture, software, text, performance
practice_description.practice_summary: American Artist examines how knowledge systems, technology, and data encode racial power structures, using surveillance, operating systems, and corporate infrastructure as both subject and material. Their legal name change to 'American Artist' is itself an intervention into how search engines, databases, and naming systems construct identity.
practice_description.methodology: American Artist works across installation, video, sculpture, and text to investigate how technology -- particularly data systems, surveillance infrastructure, and corporate platforms -- reproduces and encodes racial hierarchy. The name change (to 'American Artist' in 2013) is a foundational conceptual gesture: it disrupts search engine results, database categorization, and the assumptions embedded in naming conventions. Their research-based practice draws on critical race theory, media archaeology, and the material history of computing. Works often take the form of immersive installations that recreate or simulate the environments of technological power (server rooms, operating systems, surveillance networks).

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: American Artist's practice directly interrogates how data systems and knowledge infrastructure encode power -- the fundamental question underlying any graph-curated exhibition. Their work reveals that the structure of the graph itself (what connects to what, who is categorized how) is never neutral.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Conceptually yes -- American Artist's interventions into naming systems, databases, and search infrastructure treat the substrate layer itself as the site of critique. The work reveals that the substrate (the operating system, the database schema, the search algorithm) is always already political.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes -- the name change 'American Artist' creates relational disruptions: it changes what search results connect to what, how database records relate, and how identity is constructed through technological relationships. The work is fundamentally about how relational systems construct meaning.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Partially -- the name change creates an ongoing, evolving intervention that changes as search algorithms, databases, and cultural contexts shift. My Blue Window's simulation of Windows XP evolves in meaning as the operating system becomes more historically distant.

works.title: My Blue Window
works.description: Installation featuring a custom operating system modeled on Windows XP's interface, displayed on monitors in a dark room resembling a server room or surveillance center. The work examines how operating systems structure perception and encode corporate/racial power, referencing both the 'Blue Screen of Death' and the historical blueness of surveillance/police systems.
works.relevance: Directly demonstrates how the infrastructure layer (operating system, interface design) is a site of power and meaning-making. Essential reference for A(DAI)'s thinking about how graph infrastructure is never neutral.

works.title: Black Gooey Universe
works.description: Essay and lecture series examining the graphical user interface (GUI) as a site of racial meaning. The white desktop, the black terminal -- American Artist reads the history of computing interfaces through the lens of race, arguing that the shift from command-line (black screen) to GUI (white desktop) mirrors broader racial politics of visibility and control.
works.relevance: Foundational theoretical text for understanding how interface design and data visualization encode racial assumptions. Directly relevant to how A(DAI) designs its own interfaces and graph visualizations.

works.title: Sandy Speaks
works.description: AI chatbot trained on the writings and statements of Sandra Bland, who died in police custody. The work raises questions about voice, representation, consent, and the ethics of training AI on the words of the dead -- particularly Black people who died at the hands of the state.
works.relevance: Raises critical questions about consent, data provenance, and the ethics of AI training data that directly challenge A(DAI)'s pipeline. Whose voices are encoded? Who consented? What does it mean to train a model on someone who can no longer consent?

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: American Artist treats the protocols of everyday technology -- operating systems, search algorithms, database schemas, naming conventions -- as sites of artistic intervention and critique. The legal name change is itself a protocol hack: it disrupts the assumed protocols of identity, search, and categorization. The work does not build new protocols but reveals the politics embedded in existing ones.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: No formal system or protocol produced, but the name change 'American Artist' functions as a persistent intervention in search engine, database, and cataloguing systems -- an ongoing disruption of how technological infrastructure handles identity.

commons_orientation.licence_model: Unknown -- works are presented in institutional/gallery contexts [uncertain]
commons_orientation.commons_summary: American Artist's practice is critically engaged with questions of enclosure and openness but from a position of critique rather than infrastructure-building. The work reveals how supposedly open, universal systems (the internet, search engines, databases) actually enclose and categorize in ways that reproduce racial hierarchy. This is not commons-building but commons-questioning: who benefits from openness? Whose data is extracted?

governance_model.governance_detail: American Artist works as a solo practitioner making decisions about their own artistic practice. The work critiques governance structures (corporate, state, technological) rather than proposing alternative governance models.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Consent is a critical theme rather than an operational framework. Sandy Speaks explicitly raises the impossibility of consent when training AI on the words of someone who has died -- particularly someone who died in state custody. The work does not resolve the consent question but holds it open as an ethical wound.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship. The legal name change complicates authorship at a systemic level -- 'American Artist' as an author name disrupts attribution, cataloguing, and the infrastructure of artistic identity.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Most works are presented as fixed installations or video works. However, the name change creates a durational, continuously-evolving intervention -- its effects on search results, database entries, and cultural perception change over time as technology and context shift. Sandy Speaks was interactive (chatbot) but is not a continuously evolving system.

data_materiality.data_sources: Operating system interfaces (Windows XP), search engine results, database schemas, Sandra Bland's writings and public statements, surveillance system aesthetics, corporate technology histories.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Mixed -- some self-generated (custom operating system interfaces), some based on public/corporate materials (Windows XP, search results), some ethically complex (Sandra Bland's words used without the possibility of her consent, which is the point of the work).

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: The work engages with how semantic and relational spaces encode power -- the name 'American Artist' disrupts the embedding of identity in search and database systems. Sandy Speaks uses NLP/chatbot technology. However, the engagement is critical/conceptual rather than technically operating within ML embedding spaces.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes -- spans visual (installation, video, custom interfaces), textual (essays, chatbot), sculptural, and performative modalities, though not through a unified technical embedding space.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Works are typically presented as immersive installations in darkened gallery spaces -- server room aesthetics, multiple monitors, surveillance-like environments. My Blue Window creates a theatrical space of technological enclosure. Works have been shown at MoMA, Whitney Museum, Museum of the African Diaspora, Queens Museum, and numerous international institutions.

interoperability.composability: Low -- works are self-contained conceptual installations. The critical framework is highly composable as theory/discourse, but the artworks themselves are not designed to produce outputs that serve as inputs elsewhere.
interoperability.technical_openness: Closed -- works are institutional gallery installations, not open source or forkable. The theoretical writing is publicly accessible. [uncertain]

technical_approach.stack: Custom software (operating system simulations); NLP/chatbot technology (Sandy Speaks); video production; installation design; physical computing; web technologies [uncertain]

network_position.scene_affiliation: New York contemporary art; Black art and technology; critical race and technology studies; new media art; museum circuit (MoMA, Whitney, Queens Museum); academic discourse (taught at Carnegie Mellon, Parsons); Rhizome network; post-internet art
network_position.connections: Rhizome / ArtBase (affiliated); Hito Steyerl (shared concerns about technology and power); Trevor Paglen (surveillance and data art); Legacy Russell (glitch and identity); Danielle Brathwaite-Shirley (shared concerns about identity data governance); Simone Browne (dark surveillance studies); broader critical technology art network

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: American Artist offers A(DAI) essential critical perspective on how knowledge graphs, data infrastructure, and categorization systems are never neutral -- they encode power, reproduce hierarchy, and construct identity. Their work asks the hard questions that A(DAI) must confront: whose knowledge is centered? How does the graph's structure reproduce existing power relations? The name change alone is a case study in how database infrastructure constructs identity.
